findings.evidence: The workflow states, "Gemini can read only its cwd plus `--include-directories`", but line 22 permits shell-enabled `yolo` "in a throwaway clone or with `-s` sandbox". Following the authorized-yolo branch with only a throwaway clone leaves shell commands able to read outside those workspace roots; a clone does not isolate the host filesystem.
findings.fix: Qualify the cwd/include-directories boundary as applying to workspace-constrained file tools, not unrestricted shell commands. Require a verified sandbox or a genuinely isolated disposable container/VM without sensitive host mounts or credentials for yolo; do not treat a throwaway clone alone as isolation. Retain default approval mode when isolation cannot be established.
